category: A · Mathematical problem and canonical PINN

formulations.name: General governing physical problem
formulations.category: A · Mathematical problem and canonical PINN
formulations.meaning: States the physical relation before any neural approximation is introduced.
formulations.purpose: Defines the mathematical object that a PINN is asked to satisfy.
formulations.relation: The canonical PINN replaces the unknown field \(u\) in this problem by a trainable approximation.
formulations.symbols: \(\mathcal{F}\): governing operator; \(u\): unknown physical field; \(\boldsymbol{\lambda}\): physical coefficients; \(f\): forcing/source; \(\Omega\): spatial domain; \(T\): final time.

formulations.name: Boundary operator
formulations.category: A · Mathematical problem and canonical PINN
formulations.meaning: Represents Dirichlet, Neumann, Robin, periodic, flux, traction, radiation, or other boundary conditions through a boundary operator.
formulations.purpose: Separates the boundary statement from the interior governing equation.
formulations.relation: Boundary information can later be enforced softly through a loss or exactly through the trial space.
formulations.symbols: \(\mathcal{B}\): boundary operator; \(g_B\): prescribed boundary data; \(\partial\Omega\): domain boundary.

formulations.name: Initial condition
formulations.category: A · Mathematical problem and canonical PINN
formulations.meaning: Specifies the initial physical state for an evolutionary problem.
formulations.purpose: Selects the trajectory consistent with the governing evolution law.
formulations.relation: Canonical PINNs usually encode this statement through \(\mathcal{L}_{IC}\), unless it is imposed exactly.

formulations.name: Interface conditions
formulations.category: A · Mathematical problem and canonical PINN
formulations.meaning: Collects continuity or jump conditions across material, phase, or subdomain interfaces.
formulations.purpose: Defines how neighboring physical regions communicate.
formulations.relation: Interface conditions become explicit loss or coupling terms in multi-network and domain-decomposed PINNs.
formulations.symbols: \(\Gamma\): interface; \(u^-,u^+\): limiting states on its two sides; \(\mathcal{I}\): interface operator.

formulations.name: Observation model
formulations.category: A · Mathematical problem and canonical PINN
formulations.meaning: Represents measured data as observations of the physical state through an observation operator, potentially with noise.
formulations.purpose: Provides the empirical information needed for data-assisted forward, inverse, and assimilation tasks.
formulations.relation: The data term couples observations to the same state that is constrained by the governing physics.
formulations.symbols: \(\mathcal{H}\): observation operator; \(y^{(i)}\): measurement; \(\varepsilon^{(i)}\): measurement/model noise; \(N_d\): number of observations.

formulations.name: Canonical neural approximation
formulations.category: A · Mathematical problem and canonical PINN
formulations.meaning: Replaces the unknown state by a trainable differentiable function.
formulations.relation: This is the core coordinate/descriptor-to-field map from which residuals and losses are constructed.
formulations.symbols: \(\mathcal{N}_\theta\): neural approximation; \(\theta\): trainable neural parameters; \(\boldsymbol{\mu}\): known problem/conditioning parameters.

formulations.name: Unified input descriptor
formulations.category: A · Mathematical problem and canonical PINN
formulations.meaning: Collects space, time, parameters, geometry descriptors, controls, or other conditioning variables in one input vector.
formulations.purpose: Provides a unified notation for single-instance and parameterized PINNs.
formulations.relation: It extends the canonical coordinate input without changing the residual-learning principle.
formulations.symbols: \(\mathbf{g}\): geometry descriptor; \(\mathbf{c}\): control/operating descriptor; \(\boldsymbol{\xi}\): complete model input.

formulations.name: Vector-valued physical output
formulations.category: A · Mathematical problem and canonical PINN
formulations.meaning: Allows one network to represent several coupled physical variables or auxiliary quantities.
formulations.purpose: Expresses coupled systems, mixed variables, and multiphysics outputs.
formulations.relation: Each component can enter its own governing or compatibility residual.

formulations.name: Multilayer-perceptron realization
formulations.category: A · Mathematical problem and canonical PINN
formulations.meaning: Shows the standard fully connected realization of the trainable map.
formulations.purpose: Connects the abstract PINN ansatz with weights, biases, and activations.
formulations.relation: The PINN principle does not require this topology, but it remains the reference architecture.
formulations.symbols: \(W_\ell,\mathbf{b}_\ell\): weights and biases; \(\sigma_\ell\): activation; \(\mathbf{h}^{(\ell)}\): hidden representation.

formulations.name: Strong-form governing residual
formulations.category: A · Mathematical problem and canonical PINN
formulations.meaning: Measures pointwise violation of the governing relation by the neural field.
formulations.purpose: Creates the differentiable physics signal used in strong-form PINNs.
formulations.relation: It is the canonical bridge from the neural approximation to the physical equation.

formulations.name: Automatic-differentiation derivative
formulations.category: A · Mathematical problem and canonical PINN
formulations.meaning: Defines the derivatives of the neural trial function required by differential operators.
formulations.purpose: Links differentiable programming to residual evaluation.
formulations.relation: These derivatives are substituted into \(\mathcal{F}\) in the canonical strong form.

formulations.name: Collocation approximation of physics loss
formulations.category: A · Mathematical problem and canonical PINN
formulations.meaning: Approximates residual minimization by evaluating the physics at interior collocation points.
formulations.purpose: Turns the continuous governing statement into a trainable empirical objective.
formulations.relation: It is the canonical strong-form physics term.
formulations.symbols: \(\{(\mathbf{x}_r^{(i)},t_r^{(i)})\}_{i=1}^{N_r}\): residual collocation set; \(N_r\): number of residual points.

formulations.name: Canonical composite PINN objective
formulations.category: A · Mathematical problem and canonical PINN
formulations.meaning: Combines the physics, observations, boundary, initial, interface, and auxiliary requirements needed by a problem.
formulations.purpose: Defines the optimization target of a canonical soft-constrained PINN.
formulations.relation: Later formulations modify this objective, replace some terms, or move constraints into the representation.
formulations.symbols: \(\omega_\bullet\ge0\): loss weights; only terms relevant to the physical problem are active.
